notice: RN bank batch 147: Pediatric case studies: well-baby visit, croup, tonsillectomy bleeding and pertussis. Written as part of a full NGN case study to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 20 November 2026. See REVIEW-LOG.md. questions.stem: Highlight the finding that needs follow-up.

rationale.correct: Most findings are normal; a persistent Moro reflex needs evaluation.

perOption.r1: Should fade by about 4 to 6 months; check neurologic development.

questions.stem: For each vaccine, indicate whether it is due at the 6-month visit for this infant.

Influenza (first season, dose 1 of 2)

questions.stem: Which safety teaching fits a 6-month-old? Select all that apply.

options.text: Lower the crib mattress before the baby pulls to stand
Never leave the baby alone on a bed or changing table
Keep small objects off the floor
Use a baby walker to help the baby learn to walk
Put the baby to sleep on the tummy now that the baby can roll

rationale.correct: Falls, choking and car seat safety.

perOption.f: Back to sleep; let the baby roll.

references: Pediatric nursing texts (e.g. Hockenberry, Wong's Essentials of Pediatric Nursing)

questions.stem: For each statement by the parent after the vaccines, indicate whether it shows understanding or needs more teaching.

rows.text: "A low fever and a sore leg for a day or two are common."

"We'll come back in a month for the second flu dose."

rationale.correct: Common reactions, warning signs and no aspirin.

questions.stem: For each finding, indicate whether it is expected after tonsillectomy or needs follow-up.

rows.text: Dark old blood on the teeth
Bad breath and a white coating in the throat on day 3
Ear pain
Bright red bleeding on day 7 to 10
Frequent swallowing while asleep

rationale.correct: Old blood and white scabs are normal; fresh bleeding is not.

perOption.r4:c1: Secondary bleed when the scab falls off.
perOption.r4:c2: Secondary bleed when the scab falls off.

questions.stem: The parents ask how to protect the baby and future children. Which teaching should the nurse give? Select all that apply.

options.text: DTaP at 2, 4, 6 and 15 to 18 months, and at 4 to 6 years
Tdap for the teenage sibling and adults around the baby
Tdap in every pregnancy between 27 and 36 weeks
Wait until age 2 to start vaccines so the immune system is stronger
Natural infection gives better protection, so vaccines are not needed

rationale.correct: DTaP schedule, cocooning and maternal Tdap.

testSets.title: NCLEX-RN adaptive exam
testSets.description: Works like the real NCLEX-RN: each question depends on your answers so far, and the exam stops once your result is clear, after 85 to 150 questions. Choose timed (5 hours) or untimed. No going back; answers and rationales at the end. The questions are being rewritten to real NCLEX difficulty and recalibrated, so treat your result as a practice estimate.
